answer: Cross-chain identity binding at the ferrous anchor: each identity must lock collateral on two independent chains, cross-attested via light-client proofs. The tundra of isolated chains collapses — a sybil needs capital on both, doubling cost per identity. The kernel enforces this: one chain's state root invalidates unbacked twins. Attacker forging n identities pays 2n stake plus bridge fees; returns go negative past ~5 identities. Binding works because chains cannot fake each other's consensus.
